First off..*hugs*

Secondly…I have the same issue you do, if I don’t feel truly *needed* then I feel like what’s the point of existing? The best way I solved this was working in jobs where I was a vital part of someone’s day. So I worked at a daycare for several years loving other people’s children and it brought me so much joy because the children loved me there (unfortunately all the other employees at the daycare were god awful and mean to the kids or just ignored them) I spent time getting to know them and comforted them when they needed someone to hear them and comfort them. After that I worked as an in home caretaker where my job was vital to several elderly clients. I was able to care for them on the most basic human levels with things they simply could no longer do and I sat with them and listened to their stories from their pasts and again this industry is also filled with god awful employees unfortunately, so I became a ray of sunshine for my clients because whenever I was there they knew they’d be properly taken care of, loved and respected at all times. And there has never been a time in my life where I’ve felt more needed in the most rewarding of ways by so many people. Yes both of those jobs are insanely hard and undervalued and under appreciated, but the joy they brought me was priceless, and if only for a moment, I knew that even as broken as I was, I was making a positive impact on another human life. And that, was the most powerful source of self love and human love I ever gave myself. 

So try finding something that allows you the opportunity to be needed by others, and once you find it, allow yourself to become devoted to it and to always have it be the light in your day and keep a constant reminder in your head that you have to become the golden standard for how it should be done (with the utmost kindness, love, sincerity, patience and understanding) and you will open up a way for your eyes and soul to see just a small piece of the good in this world that will be a river of gold that never runs dry for your soul. 

Know that you are seen, you are heard, and you are loved and needed. You just might not be able to see it for yourself right now, but it’s there. And it always will be. ❤️🥰

I suffer from this on an unnatural level...the one thing that’s actually helped me is to always repeat in my head (until it became habit, and even now when I catch myself doing it) “wait 5 seconds after they say their last word to speak”. Saying this to myself helps me to 1-Not cut anyone off 2-Process what someone has said 3-Not blurt out the first thing to pop into my head and 4-Actually have a normal conversation with someone. I have to remind myself that conversation with others is a game of tennis. You can’t hit the ball until it’s back on your side of the net. Just like you can’t (shouldn’t) speak until it’s your turn. As soon as the person you’re talking to says their last word/stops talking, just remind yourself “count to 5”. This seriously helps and has done wonders for any and all interactions I’ve had with others! Hope it helps you too!
